A_target.statement:
A [[Definition:Topology|topology]] on a set $S$ is a family $\tau$ of subsets containing $\O$ and $S$, closed under arbitrary [[Definition:Set Union|unions]] and finite [[Definition:Set Intersection|intersections]].
A map $f$ is [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]] {{iff}} $\map {f^{-1} } U \in \tau$ for every open $U$.

B_source.statement: In a [[Definition:Metric Space|metric space]] $\struct {M, d}$, the [[Definition:Open Set (Metric Space)|open sets]] are the unions of open [[Definition:Open Ball|balls]], and $f$ is continuous {{iff}} the $\epsilon$-$\delta$ condition holds.

substitutions.the balls generating the open sets: the open sets themselves, taken as primitive
substitutions.the distance function: no replacement, since the axioms mention only the family of open sets
substitutions.the epsilon-delta condition: the condition that preimages of open sets are open

derived.closure under unions and finite intersec: the defining axioms, extracted from the properties balls already have
derived.the metric case: recovered by taking the topology generated by the balls

object_map.reformulation: Discard the distance function and retain only the family of sets it produced, taking their closure properties as axioms.

validity_conditions: Unions and finite intersections of open sets in a metric space are open, so the axioms are satisfied by every metric space and the generalization is faithful.
The epsilon-delta condition is equivalent to preimages of open sets being open, so continuity transfers without reference to any distance.
The generalization is strict: not every topology comes from a metric, and metrization requires separation and countability conditions that a general topology need not satisfy.
proof_plan: Arguments about continuity in metric spaces use only that open sets are closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections, and that $\O$ and $M$ are open.
Take these as the [[Definition:Topology|axioms]] for $\tau$, discarding the distance.

In a metric space, $f$ satisfies the $\epsilon$-$\delta$ condition {{iff}} $\map {f^{-1} } U$ is open for every open $U$.
Take the latter as the definition of continuity.
